newsitem.title: USA: Seer sees Q1 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Seer sees Q1 restructuring charge.

text.p: Seer Technologies Inc said on Thursday the company expected to have one more restructuring charge in the first quarter 1997, as part of its efforts to return the company to growth and profitability.

President and Chief Executive Officer Thomas Wilson also said the company, which designs, develops, markets and supports software products, planned to generate more revenue and spend less money in 1997 than it did in 1996.
"Our plan for 1997 will move us closer to our long-term goals of restoring Seer to profitability and resuming the appropriate growth trends," Wilson said.

Wilson said Seer had taken many steps to improve future results and predictability, including changing contractual arrangements with customers to spread future revenue for long-term contracts over the term of the agreement.
"While this will lower near-term revenue, it will have more positive long-term benefits by creating an annuity revenue stream with a higher degree of predictability," he said.
On the expense side, the company said it was looking at its business differently, because its software and consulting services had different management challenges and profitability models.
"We are now managing the business to address the potential impact of those two different models," Wilson said.

"We expect to record on additional restructuring charge in the first quarter, we are investing appropriately within our resources and we have intitiated margin-based compensation programs for managers in both business areas," he said.
